Firm Nandkishor Kushwah Through Its ... vs The State Of
Madhya Pradesh on 16 July, 2024
Author: Vijay Kumar Shukla
Bench: Vijay Kumar Shukla, Hirdesh 
 1   IN THE HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH  AT INDORE  BEFORE  HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE VIJAY KUMAR SHUKLA  &
 HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE HIRDESH  ON THE 16 th OF JULY, 2024  WRIT PETITION No. 5601 of 2024  FIRM NANDKISHOR KUSHWAH THROUGH ITS PROPRIETOR  NANDKISHOR KUSHWAH  Versus  THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH AND OTHERS  Appearance:
 (SHRI BHAVISHYA SHARMA, LEARNED COUNSEL FOR THE  PETITIONER)
 (SHRI BHUWAN GAUTAM, LEARNED GOVERNMENT ADVOCATE FOR  THE RESPONDENTS NO.1 TO 4/STATE)
 (SHRI AJIT KUMAR JAIN, LEARNED COUNSEL FOR THE  RESPONDENT NO.6)
 (NONE FOR RESPONDENTS NO.5 AND 7)
 ORDER Per: Vijay Kumar Shukla, J. 
The present petition is filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India whereby the e-tender submitted by the petitioner for supply of food grains, vegetables, sanitation, stationary, building construction materials and other materials etc. in Central Jail, Indore and District Jail, Indore for financial year 2023-2024 has been rejected on the ground of non-compliance of tender condition no.10 (viii).
2. The respondent no.4 had issued Notice Inviting e-tender for supply of the aforesaid material for financial year 2023-2024 for Central Jail, Indore and District Jail, Indore. The petitioner participated in the tender process and submitted e-tender which has been rejected by the impugned order. 
2 WP-5601-2024 Firm Nandkishor Kushwah Through Its ... vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10369461/
1 3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that along with the e- tender form, the petitioner has filed copy of license issued by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India, under FSS Act,
2006. Thus, it is urged that condition no.(viii) of Clause 10 of the tender notice was complied with. 
4. Learned counsel for respondents no.1 to 4 submits that the petitioner has filed incomplete copy of the license along with the e-tender form. He has invited attention of this Court to the license filed along with the reply of respondent no.6 as Annexure-A in which at the bottom it is mentioned that the license contained total 6 pages and only first page of the license was filed by the petitioner along with the e-tender form. Thus the tender form was incomplete and even with the writ petition complete copy of license has not been filed. 
5. Learned counsel for the respondents submit that the reply was filed by respondents no.1 to 4 on 28.06.2024 and by respondent no.6 on 24.05.2024 respectively, but no complete copy of license has been filed till this date. The petitioner has not filed complete copy of the license which runs into 6 pages and therefore the Committee did not take into consideration the incomplete copy of license. It is further submitted that by filing first page of the license, the condition no.10(viii) has not been complied with and the committee held that the petitioner has not complied with the condition no.10(viii) of the tender.
6. We are unable to accept the contention raised by the learned counsel for the petitioner that he has substantially complied with the condition. As per Clause 10(viii), the petitioner was required to submit copy of valid license issued under the provisions of Food Safety Standards Act, 2006. The same has to be understood that 'license' means complete copy of license. Even after filing of the replies by the respondents, the petitioner has not filed the complete copy of the license therefore,
adverse inference has to be drawn and 3 WP-5601-2024 Committee has rightly rejected the tender. 
In the contractual matters, terms and conditions of the tender has to be interpreted strictly. 
7. In view of the aforesaid, we do not find any case for interference under Article 226 of the Constitution of India. 
Accordingly, the writ petition is dismissed. 
 (VIJAY KUMAR SHUKLA) 
 JUDGE   RJ Firm Nandkishor Kushwah Through Its ... vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10369461/
